Alphabet, buoyed by cloud computing and robotics AI momentum, surged more than 6% on Friday, briefly overtaking Apple to become the world's second-most-valuable company. Apple, hit by supply chain shortages and a weaker-than-expected forecast, saw more than $350 billion wiped from its market value in a single day, slipping to third place. Nvidia, benefiting from surging AI chip demand, rebounded to a $4.86 trillion market cap, solidly retaining the top spot. Market analysts note that leadership in tech valuations has shifted from consumer electronics to AI chips and cloud computing. Alphabet is aggressively investing in AI infrastructure and has unveiled its Gemini Robotics 2 model; whether it can challenge Nvidia's dominance will be closely watched. ##### Key Elements ![AI Race Reshuffles: Alphabet Overtakes Apple in Market Cap, Vies With Nvidia for Global Crown](https://img.biggo.com/SgcCxiVTQ9DrTZdyxAaxtuswG4Fw3cGq3JDyzWKJrHs/fit/1720/0/sm/0/aHR0cHM6Ly9pbWcuYmdvLm9uZS9uZXdzLWltYWdlL2FpX2dlbmVyYXRlZC8yMDI2LTA4LzdlMzdmNDY2LTQ2ZTgtNGYwYy05ZjI0LTQxNjVmY2EzNzE4M18xNzg1NzE4ODEwX2RlZmF1bHQuanBn.webp) The artificial intelligence (AI) race continues to redraw the global tech landscape. Alphabet, Google's parent company, saw its stock surge more than 6% on Friday (July 31), briefly overtaking Apple to become the world's second-most-valuable company, trailing only AI chip leader Nvidia. Meanwhile, Apple, hit by component supply shortages and a weaker-than-expected outlook, saw more than $350 billion erased from its market value in a single day, surrendering the top spot. Alphabet's Class A shares (GOOGL) closed up $22.97, or 6.73%, at $356.65 on July 31, with trading volume reaching $16.304 billion (approximately NT$530 billion). Class C shares (GOOG) rose 6.88% in tandem. Based on market estimates using combined outstanding shares of both share classes, Alphabet's market capitalization stood at approximately $4.65 trillion to $4.67 trillion (about NT$150.8 trillion), surpassing Apple's closing market cap of roughly $4.51 trillion (about NT$145.6 trillion) by a margin of approximately $140 billion to $160 billion. Alphabet's sharp rally was supported by growth prospects in cloud computing and AI businesses, but a key catalyst was Google DeepMind's unveiling of its next-generation robotics AI model, Gemini Robotics 2. For the first time, the model uses a single system to control a humanoid robot's full-body movements, including walking, crouching, reaching, and bimanual object manipulation, while also autonomously planning multi-step tasks and collaborating with other robots. This has dramatically expanded the market's imagination regarding Alphabet's AI application footprint. Apple (AAPL), by contrast, was dragged down by memory and chip supply constraints that weighed on its guidance. Shares plunged $24.52, or 7.35%, to close at $308.91 on July 31 — the steepest single-day drop since March 2020, when the pandemic triggered a global market selloff. Measured by post-earnings stock reaction, this was also Apple's worst earnings-day performance since a 8% decline on January 28, 2014. Infra & Chips.content: IT Brief Asia - Technology news for CIOs & IT decision-makers [![IT Brief Asia logo](/brands/itb-new-logo.svg)](/) [Powered By ![TechDay logo](/brands/td-new-logo-right.svg)](https://techday.asia) ![Google expands AI infrastructure with Lustre & C4N](https://itbrief.asia/uploads/story/2026/08/03/bikash-koley-and-arjun-singh-story-312724.webp) [Cloud Security](https://itbrief.asia/tag/cloud-security) [DC](https://itbrief.asia/tag/data-centers) [HPC](https://itbrief.asia/tag/high-performance-computing) # Google expands AI infrastructure with Lustre & C4N Mon, 3rd Aug 2026 (Today) [![Sean Mitchell](https://itbrief.asia/rails/active_storage/representations/redirect/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsiZGF0YSI6MTYyOSwicHVyIjoiYmxvYl9pZCJ9fQ==--a929a91c2a04d9af95ed98b14ed4d405bc70c1a7/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsiZGF0YSI6eyJmb3JtYXQiOiJ3ZWJwIiwicmVzaXplX3RvX2ZpbGwiOlsxNjAsMTYwXSwicXVhbGl0eSI6ODV9LCJwdXIiOiJ2YXJpYXRpb24ifX0=--89ddf5e6765c65a563c2258053e9d33c05d195da/IMG_3092.webp) SEAN MITCHELL Publisher](/author/sean-mitchell) Google Cloud has moved its Managed Lustre storage service into general availability and has also made its C4N network- and storage-optimised virtual machines generally available. The updates are part of a broader monthly round-up of additions to Google's AI infrastructure portfolio. Managed Lustre is offered in four performance tiers, ranging from 125 MB/s to 1000 MB/s per TiB of capacity, and can scale to 8 PB of storage. The service uses DDN's EXAScaler technology. C4N is Google's first virtual machine series designed specifically for network- and block storage-heavy workloads. The machines use 5th Gen Intel Xeon Scalable processors and Google's Titanium hardware. Google cited 400 Gbps network bandwidth, 95 million packets per second and up to 25 GiB/s of block storage throughput when used with Hyperdisk Extreme. Google also raised the upper size limit for standard Google Kubernetes Engine clusters using Dataplane V2 with network policies enabled. The service now supports clusters of up to 15,000 nodes, a scale aimed at large corporate, AI and machine learning deployments. Another change focused on the use of expensive accelerator hardware. A co-operative time-slicing feature in llm-d allows reinforcement learning workloads to interleave separate jobs on shared physical systems, raising accelerator duty cycles from about 40% to 70% without affecting model convergence or accuracy. **Security and tooling** Google has also open-sourced k8s-aibom, a Kubernetes controller intended to identify AI runtimes running in container clusters and create CycloneDX machine learning bills of materials. The tool is intended to help organisations track AI software components inside Google Kubernetes Engine environments. Google also highlighted several developer and operations guides tied to its TPU and Kubernetes services. These include support materials for Moonshot AI's Kimi K3 open-weight model, guidance on running Ray on TPUs, a microbenchmark suite for TPU performance testing, and instructions for using GKE Agent Sandbox and Pod snapshots to increase the number of AI agents that can run on a fixed compute footprint. The update also pointed to a technical blueprint describing inference work for Mistral 3 Large on Ironwood, also known as TPU v7x. According to Google, engineering changes including hybrid sharding, tree reductions and asynchronous scheduling produced a 1.5x performance gain and increased throughput by up to 48% while maintaining benchmark accuracy neutrality. **Market positioning** Alongside the product releases, Google drew attention to external and internal research on AI infrastructure demand. It said Gartner had named it a Leader in its inaugural Magic Quadrant for AI Infrastructure and placed it highest for Ability to Execute and furthest for Completeness of Vision. This strategic move aims to reduce the company's reliance on smartphones and target the growing AI chip market, with initial production slated for Q4. * [ETDatacenters](/agency/88676092/ETDatacenters "ETDatacenters") * Published On Aug 03, 2026 at 07:16 AM IST * [![Google Preference icon](https://img.etb2bimg.com/files/cp/6e49a4e9b325074f01a6.png)](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=datacenters.economictimes.indiatimes.com "Select ETDatacenters as Preferred Choice on Google") Select ETDatacenters as Preferred Choice on Google ## Highlights * MediaTek approves $5 billion for AI application-specific integrated circuits (ASICs) for data centers. * The company aims to shift focus from smartphones to custom AI chips for cloud providers. * First AI accelerator ASIC production expected in Q4, with a second-generation chip by early 2028. * MediaTek projects over $2 billion in data center AI chip revenue by 2026. Taiwanese fabless chipmaker [MediaTek](/tag/mediatek) announced on Thursday that its board has approved a $5 billion discretionary financing budget. This allocation is intended to support the company's long-term expansion into artificial intelligence (AI) application-specific integrated circuits ([ASICs](/tag/asics)) designed for [data centers](/tag/data+centers). MediaTek Chief Executive Officer (CEO) [Rick Tsai](/tag/rick+tsai) stated during the company's second-quarter (2Q26) earnings call that this flexible framework provides optionality to support long-term growth and capitalise on significant data center opportunities. The initiative underscores MediaTek's strategy to reduce its reliance on smartphone chip sales and establish itself as a major supplier of custom chips to cloud companies. ### Market Opportunity and Production Timeline MediaTek has revised its estimate for the addressable market for custom [AI chips](/tag/ai+chips) in 2027 to $80 billion, an increase from its earlier projection of $70-80 billion. The company also raised its target market share to 15-20%, up from the previous 10-15%. Tsai confirmed that MediaTek's first AI accelerator ASIC is scheduled to commence production in the fourth quarter. A second-generation chip is anticipated to enter volume production in early 2028. MediaTek projects its data-center AI chip business to generate over $2 billion in revenue in 2026. Rival American chipmaker [Qualcomm](/tag/qualcomm) is also expanding into the AI data center market, targeting $5 billion in revenue from this segment by fiscal year 2027 and $15 billion by 2029. ### Impact on Smartphone Segment In the second quarter, MediaTek's mobile phone segment revenue saw a 20% year-on-year decline. This was attributed to increasing bill-of-materials costs, driven by an AI-linked component crunch. Tsai noted that the company's outlook for global smartphone shipments remains unchanged, with an expected market decline of about 15% in units this year. Preliminary estimates from [Counterpoint Research](/tag/counterpoint+research) indicate that global smartphone shipments fell 11% year-on-year in Q2 2026, reaching the lowest second-quarter levels since 2013. The research firm highlighted that memory and storage prices continued to inflate through the quarter as memory suppliers prioritised AI data center demand over consumer electronics, leading vendors to pass rising costs to consumers through price hikes, particularly affecting entry-to-mid-tier devices. ## Comments ![Comment](/_icons/images/et-default-user.svg) What are your thoughts?
